scenarios.title: Recover an existing Midnight wallet root behind native user presence

targetPlans.note: Use only to inspect recovery navigation, validation, and lifecycle clearing; desktop authorization is explicitly non-production.
Preferred demo target. Use run as the one-command path, or build then deploy when reusing an exact artifact; do not execute both paths redundantly.
Run only on a disposable emulator; the harness changes the device PIN and refuses physical devices.
Useful for diagnosis on macOS, but simulator LocalAuthentication is not physical Face ID evidence.
Do not claim or attempt physical iOS deployment until signing, provisioning, and device policy are implemented.

manualSteps: On physical Android, select recovery for an empty PreProd profile, enter a non-production 64-character lowercase hexadecimal root, confirm the operation, and deny native authorization. Confirm recovery fails without creating an account and the root field is cleared.
Enter the non-production root again, approve with the configured device credential or biometric, and confirm account 0/address 0 is ready or is reported as separately retryable.
Attempt recovery again for the initialized profile. Confirm the wallet refuses to replace or merge custody before consuming another root.
While owner input is present, background and resume the app or cancel recovery. Confirm the root and confirmation are cleared before another attempt.
expectedOutcomes: Denial installs no root and remains safely retryable.
Approval installs the root only into empty protected custody and derives the canonical account independently.
Initialized custody rejects a duplicate import.
Lifecycle changes clear owner input and confirmation.

testMapping.manual: Physical Android executes the four root-recovery acceptance steps; desktop is preflight and simulators are diagnostic.
testMapping.planned: Automate receipt-scoped physical Android evidence only after its device-input and privacy boundary is reviewed.

scenarios.title: Synchronize a development-only standalone Midnight profile

targetPlans.note: The diagnostic harness owns an emulator-only localhost composition and its scoped app-data/port cleanup. Loopback transport is not Tailnet routing or a public network.
The simulator reaches the same loopback-only standalone composition. Its result is diagnostic and does not establish physical-device or public-network behavior.

Physical Android is a manual development-route diagnostic only: the launcher selects one host MagicDNS identity at build time and rejects emulator routing. Tailnet TLS does not make this a public Midnight network or production acceptance.

manualSteps: For a supported local target, use the reviewed standalone-local diagnostic harness; it creates a fresh protected profile and verifies only that the account reaches Live/Synced live-source state with unshielded and shielded receive rails.

For the physical Android Tailnet diagnostic, the operator first authorizes one device and the owned Tailnet stack, then launches the reviewed compile-time profile. In Settings, confirm the closed deployment card reports undeployed and route class tailnet without revealing or selecting an endpoint.

In Wallet, select the explicitly offered public demo wallet only when demonstrating its public development authority, activate its protected account, and use Sync now. Confirm public NIGHT refresh, DUST synchronization, and shielded synchronization remain independently truthful rather than inferring one from another.

Record only the closed freshness/result states. Do not claim a particular NIGHT, DUST, shielded-note, or shielded-token balance: the public-genesis development state is mutable and the scenario neither funds nor spends it.
Stop the owned standalone stack and, on physical Android, follow the existing operator-authorized app-data cleanup boundary.
expectedOutcomes: The selected build reports only the fixed undeployed network and its compiled local or Tailnet route class; no runtime picker, endpoint disclosure, or public-deployment claim appears.

A successful account refresh and each successful DUST/shielded session report live-source state independently. Cached, cancelled, stalled, unavailable, or failed sessions are not promoted to live or spend-ready.
Both receive-address rails can be present after protected account activation, but their presence and any displayed values do not prove current balances, funding, settlement, or production authority.
Localhost and Tailnet runs remain development diagnostics; the physical Tailnet route is not production or public-network acceptance evidence.

testMapping.manual: Physical Android Tailnet routing and the independent visible NIGHT/DUST/shielded freshness states require the bounded manual steps; no device identifier, Tailnet name, route, credential, or balance is retained as evidence.
testMapping.planned: No automated physical Android Tailnet asset-sync receipt exists, and no scenario claims a public Midnight deployment or funded-balance acceptance.

scenarios.title: Run a bounded native development proof benchmark

targetPlans.note: Native desktop is the only reviewed inventory target. The scenario admits one operator-selected low-k proof, not a sweep, high-k run, public resource sample, simulator result, or physical-device measurement.

manualSteps: Approve the possible download of public proving parameters and the temporary-cache disk budget, then use the reviewed build and run commands. Confirm the panel labels itself development-only and shows process RSS/CPU as unavailable because no reviewed public sampler exists.

Select Circuit k=1 and choose Run once. Wait for a completed report containing realized k, measured rows and hashes, key-generation time, proving time, verification time, and proof bytes; record no endpoint, cache path, identifier, or proof bytes.

Do not use Run sequential sweep in this bounded demo. The default sweep ends at k=17, but ordinary-k sweeps and every k=18 through k=21 run require a separate resource decision; high-k also requires the visible acknowledgement and an owner-invoked resource receipt.
Stop the foreground desktop process. Retain the public parameter cache for reuse by default, or explicitly remove only the app-private benchmark cache when disk policy requires it.
expectedOutcomes: Exactly one admitted worker produces a locally verified k=1 synthetic-proof report, while the UI remains responsive and a second worker cannot be admitted concurrently.
The result is process-local diagnostic measurement, not a performance budget, regression baseline, release gate, public resource sample, or acceptance claim.
High-k remains separately acknowledged and owner-receipted; no simulator, physical-device, thermal, battery, native-custody, or release evidence is established.

testMapping.manual: An authorized desktop operator runs only k=1 and inspects the verified process-local result; no simulator or physical-device lane is claimed.
testMapping.planned: There is no receipt-scoped performance, public resource-sampling, high-k, simulator, physical Android, or physical iOS demonstration. A real-device high-k measurement needs a separate owner resource receipt and remains evidence rather than a merge or acceptance gate.

scenarios.title: Inspect and clear payload-free diagnostics through the headless API

targetPlans.note: Headless NDJSON gives deterministic protocol evidence for one process. It is not a rendered UI, persistent log, telemetry stream, or device claim.

manualSteps: Start the headless target and submit one deliberately invalid, fixed, non-sensitive line so the process records headless.request.rejected without echoing the input.
Submit system.diagnostics.snapshot with empty parameters. Confirm the newest event exposes only sequence, fixed code, and severity, and that payloadsRetained is false.
Submit system.diagnostics.clear only with confirmed=true and intent=CLEAR_LOCAL_DIAGNOSTICS, then take another snapshot and confirm the retained count is zero.
Stop the foreground process; do not retain the transient output as a user activity history or durable support journal.
expectedOutcomes: The snapshot reports bounded retained, total, and evicted counts plus closed code/severity values without echoing the rejected input.
Clear fails closed without the exact confirmation and empties only the current process ring when authorized.
Process exit removes all diagnostic state; no persistence, upload, arbitrary field, timestamp, endpoint, or benchmark telemetry is implied.

testMapping.manual: The operator may repeat the same fixed non-sensitive NDJSON sequence; the automated contract is the authoritative preflight.
testMapping.planned: This scenario intentionally does not provide persistent support storage or a rendered mobile/desktop claim.

scenarios.title: Inspect the bounded local diagnostics screen

targetPlans.note: Desktop renders the user-facing filters and clear confirmation. Empty process state is valid; this target does not manufacture failures or claim device behavior.

manualSteps: Open Settings, choose Diagnostics, and confirm the page describes telemetry as off and the ring as payload-free and process-local.
Inspect retained, total, evicted, and capacity counts, Warning and Error filters, fixed-code search, and newest-first rows. An empty ring is a valid clean state.
If events exist, search only a fixed code and exercise the filters. Open Clear local events, cancel once, then explicitly confirm clearing and verify the empty state.
Stop the foreground desktop process; never treat visible rows or screenshots as persisted user activity, benchmark telemetry, or a durable support journal.
expectedOutcomes: The screen exposes only bounded counts, fixed codes, severity labels, sequence order, filters, and explicit clearing.
Unknown search text cannot project arbitrary payloads, and canceling the clear confirmation preserves the ring.
The desktop result is diagnostic UI evidence only; it does not establish mobile, release, native-custody, or durable-support behavior.

testMapping.manual: Desktop inspection covers rendered controls and empty or populated presentation without claiming device evidence.
testMapping.planned: No simulator or physical-device diagnostics-screen receipt is currently claimed.

Oxid demonstrates the bounded Final Portal Digital Passport journey from review and explicit consent through verified encrypted storage, restart, and fresh reverification, while keeping localhost, virtual mobile, and physical Android Tailnet evidence distinct and development-only.
